results.coordinate_gate: Under all actual159 and fixed-axis quartic163 hypotheses, every nonconstant invariant of original weight<=4 is an actual polynomial coordinate. The full initial ideal gives the entire weight4 ansatz. Its cubic time coefficient forces the normalized coefficient pair C_Z and X+zeta. A nonzero residual slope gives a nondegenerate original critical point, contradicting the global E slice. A zero residual constant gives an invariant suspension of a quartic, contradicted by the integral-intercept normality argument. The remaining case has an explicit polynomial inverse.
results.necessary_coefficient: With chi=c1*tau+c0, k=r*rho+k0, existence of such an invariant forces chi*k0 in C[tau] of degree<=4. This is necessary only; the lower time coefficients have not been solved. No uniform existence is claimed.
results.exact_field: K=ker_L partial_rho is finite over C(tau). The completed163 coefficient equations put all projected coordinates in K(rho)[y]. Actual field return then forces L=K(rho). K is not asserted rational and no integral coordinate equality follows.
results.contracted_primes: The actual chart gives k in S_a and eta=rho-chi*k in S_a intersect K. A polynomial annihilator Q(T,V) of eta can be normalized so q0(V)=Q(tau0,V)!=0. Polynomial substitution proves q0(rho) in g*S_a, g=a*chi. Every prime of S containing g but avoiding a sends (tau,rho) to one of a fixed finite set of complex points. This proof needs no finite-generation or smooth-surface theorem; the a=0 locus and multiplicity bounds remain open.
